body.statement: In the continuous extension \(\nu\downarrow0\), the treatment diffusion reduces to the control Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process, \(m_\gamma\to0\), and \(V_\gamma\to2\lambda\tau/(\lambda+\tau)^3\).  For fixed \(N\) and an interior implemented capacity, the exact prelimit Poisson martingale yields the ordinary finite-state occupation central limit theorem as \(T_N\to\infty\).  This second assertion is an internal reduction for the equal-arm stationary homogeneous subclass; it is compatible with, but does not transfer a positive result to, the cited broader model allowing distinct arm populations and capacity.
body.justification: The reductions verify the unconstrained diffusion formula and the internally derived fixed-state-space limit.
body.gap: They are fidelity checks and make no upward transfer claim.
body.consumer: Readers can compare against closed-form Ornstein--Uhlenbeck and finite-state benchmarks.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(\lambda,\tau>0\) and take the continuous extension \(\nu\downarrow0\).  Then \(D\to d\), \(q=\lambda(\tau+\nu)/D\to\lambda\tau/d=q_0\), and
\[
 -dx-\nu\min(x,\gamma)\longrightarrow-dx
\]
uniformly on compact sets.  The two pieces of \(\pi_\gamma\) coalesce into the Gaussian density \(\pi_0\).  Their quadratic exponents have a common integrable Gaussian envelope for \(\nu\) in a compact neighborhood of zero, so dominated convergence gives \(m_\gamma\to0\).  The Poisson flux formula and \(1/D\leq h_\gamma'\leq1/d\) similarly give \(h_\gamma'\to d^{-1}\) in stationary \(L^2\).  Therefore
\[
 V_\gamma=2q\int(h_\gamma')^2\pi_\gamma
 \longrightarrow 2q_0/d^2
 =\frac{2\lambda\tau}{(\lambda+\tau)^3}.                        \tag{50}
\]

Now hold \(N\) and an interior capacity fixed.  The chain is finite and irreducible, its exact flux solution is bounded, and (39) expresses the centered occupation integral as a bounded-endpoint term plus a jump martingale.  The finite-state ergodic theorem follows directly from the spectral expansion used in (10), so the normalized predictable bracket converges to the exact stationary Poisson energy.  The normalized jumps are bounded by a constant times \(T_N^{-1/2}\); applying the conditional expansion (47) gives the scalar Gaussian occupation limit as \(T_N\to\infty\).  This proves the internal fixed-system reduction.  Lemma \(\mathrm{boutilier\mbox{-}anchor\mbox{-}scope}\) records that the published anchor permits distinct arm populations and capacity, so compatibility is asserted without claiming that this subclass proof transfers upward.
